newsitem.title: LATVIA: BUDGET DEFICIT POSSIBILE - FIN MIN.
newsitem.headline: BUDGET DEFICIT POSSIBILE - FIN MIN.

text.p: Finance Minister Roberts Zile said on Thursday that Latvia could have a budget deficit of around ten million lats this year because individual income tax revenues will probably fall short of target.
"If the budget deficit of around 10 to 12 million lats is there at the year end, it will make up less than 0.4 percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP)," Zile told a news conference.
Zile said the current surplus of 35 million lats could be cancelled by public sector expenditures of 31 million lats which have been allocated but not spent yet.
"We are still close to zero when we balance the real income with the planned expenditure," Zile said.
The government had originally targeted a balanced budget and the figures to date suggested that goal was on track.
Out-going Prime Minister Andris Shkele earlier said that the budget was showing a healthy surplus.
But Zile said a deficit could appear if tax collection did not improve drastically.
"If income tax and value added tax collection or other no-tax income does not improve drastically during the rest of 1997, we might face a slight deficit," Zile said.
The planned budget expenditure for the first half of 1997 was 284.59 million lats and the actual figure came to 252.99 million lats, Zile said.
Individual income tax, received by local municipalities and the health care sector, was targeted to bring in 189 million lats.
"The government has already lent the municipalities 8.7 million lats through the local government equalisation fund to cover the gap in the tax collection," Zile said.
Zile added that "high-ranking officials have been manipulating the figures," but he declined to mention any names.
